group.title: Nature and the environment
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: Things you throw away because you don’t want them.
examples: Please put your {trash} in the bin.
wrong: She threw away the trash because she wanted to keep it.

words.meaning: A light, strong material made from oil, used for bottles and bags.
examples: This bottle is made of {plastic}.
wrong: Plastic is a kind of fruit that grows on trees.

words.meaning: Power from things like electricity or gas that makes machines work.
examples: Turn off the lights to save {energy}.
wrong: The heater uses no energy, but it makes the room hot.

words.meaning: Electricity made from the light of the sun.
examples: Our school uses {solar power} from panels on the roof.
wrong: Solar power is made by burning coal at night.

words.meaning: Electricity made when moving air turns big machines.
examples: Those tall white towers make {wind power}.
wrong: Wind power works best on days when the air does not move at all.

words.meaning: The gray or black cloud that comes from something burning.
examples: Black {smoke} came out of the factory chimney.
wrong: Smoke is clear water that falls from the sky.

words.meaning: To keep a thing and put it to work again rather than throw it away.
examples: I {reuse} glass jars to store rice.
wrong: She reuses her paper cups by throwing them away after one drink.

words.meaning: Connected with the air, water and land around us.
examples: Pollution is a big {environmental} problem.
wrong: Our biggest environmental problem is that my phone is too slow.

words.meaning: To use less electricity, gas or fuel.
examples: We {save energy} by turning off lights we are not using.
wrong: He saves energy by leaving the heater on all night.

words.meaning: A hard black rock that is burned to make heat or electricity.
examples: Burning {coal} makes the air dirty.
wrong: Coal is a soft white powder used to make cakes.

words.meaning: To make a tree fall by cutting it.
examples: They {cut down} the old trees to build houses.
wrong: They cut down the tree, and it is still standing tall.

words.meaning: Dirty or harmful gases and smoke in the air.
examples: Cars and factories cause a lot of {air pollution}.
wrong: The air pollution was so low that the air was the cleanest ever.

words.meaning: Made dirty and harmful by waste, smoke or chemicals.
examples: Nobody can swim in the river because it is {polluted}.
wrong: The polluted lake was so clean that we drank from it.

words.meaning: A large white bear that lives near the North Pole.
examples: {Polar bears} hunt on the ice for seals.
wrong: Polar bears live in hot deserts with no ice.

words.meaning: An animal with a hard shell that lives in or near water.
examples: A sea {turtle} swam slowly past the boat.
wrong: The turtle flew over the trees on its wings.

words.meaning: A plant like a small tree with many branches.
examples: A bird made its nest in the {bush}.
wrong: The bush is taller than the highest tree in the forest.

words.meaning: An area of land covered with trees, smaller than a forest.
examples: We walked through the {woods} to the lake.
wrong: The woods had no trees at all.

words.meaning: A large, hard piece of stone.
examples: We sat on a big {rock} by the river.
wrong: The rock was so soft that it melted in my hand.

words.meaning: One of the colored parts of a flower.
examples: The rose has soft red {petals}.
wrong: The petal is the part of a tree under the ground.

words.meaning: A plant with sharp points that grows in hot, dry places.
examples: A {cactus} can live for months without rain.
wrong: A cactus needs lots of water and grows best in the snow.

words.meaning: A very tall plant with a big round yellow head and black seeds.
examples: The {sunflowers} in the field were taller than me.
wrong: A sunflower is a tiny blue plant that grows in the dark.

words.meaning: One of the soft, light things that cover a bird’s body.
examples: A white {feather} fell from the bird’s wing.
wrong: The feather was so heavy that I couldn’t lift it.

words.meaning: The bright light that comes down from the sky during the day.
examples: Plants need {sunlight} to grow.
wrong: We sat in the warm sunlight in the middle of the night.

words.meaning: Coming from plants, animals or the earth, not made by people or machines.
examples: The park has a {natural} lake, not one made by people.
wrong: The plastic flowers look nice, and they are completely natural.

words.meaning: The gas in the air that people and animals need to breathe.
examples: Trees give us the {oxygen} we breathe.
wrong: We need oxygen, so we try never to breathe.

words.meaning: A flying insect that makes honey and can sting.
examples: A {bee} landed on the flower.
wrong: The bee gave milk to its babies.

words.meaning: An insect with large, colorful wings.
examples: A yellow {butterfly} sat on a flower.
wrong: The butterfly swam to the bottom of the sea.

words.meaning: A wild animal like a large dog that lives and hunts in groups.
examples: We heard a {wolf} howling in the forest.
wrong: The wolf is a small fish that lives in ponds.

words.meaning: A wild animal like a small dog with red fur and a thick tail.
examples: A {fox} ran across the field at night.
wrong: The fox has green feathers and lays eggs in trees.

words.meaning: A wild animal with long legs; the males often have horns like branches.
examples: We saw a {deer} eating grass at the edge of the woods.
wrong: The deer flew up into the sky.

words.meaning: A very large animal that lives in the sea and breathes air.
examples: A huge {whale} came up out of the water.
wrong: The whale is so small it can sit in your hand.

words.meaning: A clever, friendly sea animal like a small whale.
examples: {Dolphins} jumped in the waves next to our boat.
wrong: Dolphins live in trees in the desert.

words.meaning: A large fish with sharp teeth.
examples: The {shark} swam fast toward the smaller fish.
wrong: The shark climbed the mountain to find food.

words.meaning: A small green animal with long back legs that jumps and lives near water.
examples: A {frog} jumped into the pond.
wrong: The frog has wings and flies high above the clouds.

words.meaning: A large bird with strong wings that hunts small animals.
examples: An {eagle} flew high above the mountains.
wrong: The eagle is a tiny insect that lives in the grass.

words.meaning: A bird with big eyes that hunts at night.
examples: We heard an {owl} hooting in the dark.
wrong: The owl sleeps all night and hunts at noon.

words.meaning: A small animal with a long thick tail that climbs trees and eats nuts.
examples: A {squirrel} buried a nut in the garden.
wrong: The squirrel is a large animal that lives in the sea.

words.meaning: A small animal with eight legs that makes webs.
examples: A {spider} made a web in the corner.
wrong: The spider has two legs and sings in the morning.

words.meaning: An accident when oil comes out of a ship and covers the sea.
examples: The {oil spill} killed many sea birds.
wrong: After the oil spill, the beach was cleaner than ever.

words.meaning: An animal that lives free in nature, not with people.
examples: Lions are {wild animals} that live in Africa.
wrong: My pet cat is a wild animal that sleeps on my bed.
